$comment: The release gate policy (Gate 4, ledger ENG-071, ENG-079). A build is classified by its CONFIGURATION, never by what someone calls it: demo flag on and noindex on is the demonstration channel; anything else (demo off, or indexable) is client-production. The gate then requires everything listed for that channel. No channel may deploy: deployment needs its own recorded approval for the exact commit, and no tool in this repository deploys anything.

demonstration.meaning: the fictional Jade & Ember showcase: flags.demo true, seo.noindex true. It may be packaged as a preview for review. It may never be indexed or sold as a client site.

client-production.meaning: any build with flags.demo false or seo.noindex false: a real client site, indexable, with production metadata.

deployment: never performed by any tool here; a deployment approval row for the exact commit and channel is recorded for information, and the gate reports it, but nothing acts on it

approvalRows.release-approval: Type contains release-approval; the Decision text contains `channel: <channel>`, `version: <x.y.z>` and `commit: <40 hex>` that equal the build being released
approvalRows.rights-verification: Type contains rights-verification; the Decision text names who verified, the sources reviewed and the date (docs/JADE_AND_EMBER_MEDIA_RIGHTS_POLICY.md)
approvalRows.deployment-approval: Type contains deployment-approval; the Decision text contains `channel:` and `commit:` like a release approval

evidence.$comment: JSON files in engineering/release/evidence/. They are human or tool records of work the automated checks cannot do. Each: { type, commit, date, by, summary, url? , conclusion? }. commit must equal the release commit for ci-run; the others must name the release commit or an earlier one for the same version.

types.real-device: at least one iPhone and one Android phone, recorded by a person
types.screen-reader: NVDA, VoiceOver and TalkBack passes on all five pages, recorded by a person
types.browser-matrix: automated and manual results in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (decision D-11: Firefox and WebKit are tested before production deployment)
types.ci-run: a GitHub Actions run of the verify workflow for the release commit with conclusion success, with its URL
